section_1_complete_textbook_notes.chapter_overview: This chapter develops fundamental geometry concepts starting from primitive elements (point, line segment, ray, line) to angles and their quantitative measurement in degrees (°). It explores rotation turns (full turn = 360°, straight angle = 180°, right angle = 90°), angle classification (acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex), angle measurement using a protractor, paper-folding constructions for perpendiculars and angle bisectors, and geometric properties of intersecting lines.

detailed_sections.section_number_title: 2.1 Points, Line Segments, Rays, and Lines
detailed_sections.full_textbook_explanation: A Point marks an exact location in space with no length, width, or depth. A Line Segment is a straight path connecting two distinct endpoints, possessing a definite length. A Ray originates at an endpoint and extends endlessly in one direction. A Line extends infinitely in two opposite directions.

mathematical_definitions.formal_definition: A precise location in a plane represented by a dot, having zero dimensions.
The shortest straight path between two distinct points A and B, denoted AB.
A straight portion of a line that begins at an initial point and continues indefinitely in one direction, denoted ray AB.
mathematical_definitions.example: Sunlight rays originating from the Sun.

mathematical_definitions.formal_definition: A continuous one-dimensional straight path extending infinitely in both directions, denoted line AB or l.
mathematical_definitions.example: Line l passing through points A and B.

formulas_and_properties.name: Uniqueness of Line through Two Points
formulas_and_properties.statement_or_expression: Exactly one unique straight line passes through two distinct points.
formulas_and_properties.variable_definitions: A, B = distinct points in a plane
formulas_and_properties.direct_example: Points P and Q define exactly line PQ.

detailed_sections.full_textbook_explanation: An Angle is formed by two rays meeting at a common initial vertex. Angle size measures the amount of rotation required to turn one ray onto the other. A complete rotation equals 360 degrees (360°). Half a rotation forms a straight angle (180°). One-quarter of a rotation forms a right angle (90°).

mathematical_definitions.formal_definition: The figure formed by two rays, called the arms or legs of the angle, sharing a common endpoint called the vertex.
mathematical_definitions.example: Angle AOB with vertex O and arms OA and OB.

mathematical_definitions.formal_definition: An angle measuring exactly 90 degrees, formed by a quarter turn.
mathematical_definitions.example: Corner angle of a rectangular sheet.

formulas_and_properties.name: Fractional Turn to Degree Formula
formulas_and_properties.statement_or_expression: Angle (°) = Fraction of Full Turn x 360°
formulas_and_properties.variable_definitions: Fraction of Turn = proportion of 1 full rotation

detailed_sections.full_textbook_explanation: Angles are classified by degree measure: Acute Angle (0° < theta < 90°), Right Angle (theta = 90°), Obtuse Angle (90° < theta < 180°), Straight Angle (theta = 180°), Reflex Angle (180° < theta < 360°).

mathematical_definitions.formal_definition: An angle whose measure is strictly greater than 0° and strictly less than 90°.
An angle whose measure is strictly greater than 90° and strictly less than 180°.

section_2_step_by_step_algorithms.method_name: Measuring an Angle with a Protractor
step_by_step_instructions: Step 1: Place the center baseline point of the protractor directly over the angle vertex.
Step 2: Align one arm of the angle precisely along the 0° baseline mark.
Step 3: Read the degree mark where the second arm crosses the circular protractor scale, selecting the scale (inner or outer) that started at 0° on the aligned arm.

model_textbook_example.problem: Determine the measure of angle AOB where arm OA aligns with 0° on the inner scale and arm OB crosses at 65°.
working_steps: Step 1: Vertex O aligned with protractor center.
Step 2: Arm OA aligned with 0° inner scale.
Step 3: Arm OB points to 65° on inner scale.

section_3_in_text_boxes_and_try_these.question_text: The Ashoka Chakra has 24 spokes. What is the angle between any pair of adjacent spokes?
section_3_in_text_boxes_and_try_these.complete_solution: Total angle of a complete circle = 360°. The 24 spokes divide 360° into 24 equal central angles. Angle between adjacent spokes = 360° / 24 = 15°.

section_4_complete_textbook_exercise_sol.question_text: How many right angles are formed when a straight line crease on paper is folded onto itself?
solution_steps: Step 1: Folding a straight line crease onto itself creates a perpendicular crease intersecting the original line.
Step 2: Intersecting perpendicular lines form 4 adjacent right angles (90° each) around the point of intersection.
